description: MO medium + 30 mM sodium lactate / 20 mM sodium sulfite (respiratory) — medium reported in PMC8794893 (complex/undefined base — extracts not BiGG-mappable).

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC8794893 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Full recipe recovered from the primary literature: base medium 'MO (Missouri) medium' (Zane GM, Yen HB, Wall JD. 2010. Effect of the deletion of qmoABC and the promoter-distal gene encoding a hypothetical protein on sulfate reduction in Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. Appl Environ Microbiol 76:5500-5509. PMID:20581180; DOI:10.1128/AEM.00691-10. Full verbatim recipe (modified from Zane et al. 2010) also given in Rajeev et al. 2020, Front Microbiol 11:610455, DOI:10.3389/fmicb.2020.610455 an
provenance.verification_evidence: Under respiratory conditions, 15 or 30 mM sodium lactate was added as the electron donor, and sodium sulfate (30 mM), sodium sulfite (10 or 20 mM) or sodium thiosulfate (10 or 20 mM) was added as the terminal electron acceptor.
provenance.recipe_evidence: Paper: 'D. vulgaris H WT and the two modified strains were grown anaerobically at 37 C in MO medium. Under respiratory conditions, 15 or 30 mM sodium lactate was added as the electron donor, and sodium sulfate (30 mM), sodium sulfite (10 or 20 mM) or sodium thiosulfate (10 or 20 mM) was added as the terminal electron acceptor.' Base MO medium (modified from Zane et al. 2010), verbatim from Rajeev et al. 2020: '8 mM magnesium chloride, 20 mM ammonium chloride, 0.6 mM calcium chloride, 2 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.2), 30 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.4)' plus '6 ml/L trace elements, 1 ml/L vitamin solution,
provenance.base_medium_reference: Zane GM, Yen HB, Wall JD. 2010. Effect of the deletion of qmoABC and the promoter-distal gene encoding a hypothetical protein on sulfate reduction in Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. Appl Environ Microbiol 76:5500-5509. PMID:20581180; DOI:10.1128/AEM.00691-10. Full verbatim recipe (modified from Zane et al. 2010) also given in Rajeev et al. 2020, Front Microbiol 11:610455, DOI:10.3389/fmicb.2020.610455 and in Fels et al. 2023, Front Microbiol 14:1095191 (PMC10102598). Vitamin solution per Brandis & Thauer 1981, J Gen Microbiol 126:249-252.

components.mapping_note: [CHEM-B12-01] cbl1 is Cob(I)alamin, the transient reduced Co(I) intracellular redox state of the cofactor -- it is not a dietary or medium B12 species. Cyanocobalamin (C63H88CoN14O14P) has no in_biggr BiGG id (b12 carries no formula and no InChIKey and is absent from BiGGr). adocbl (Adenosylcobalamin, C72H100CoN18O17P, ZIHHMGTYZOSFRC-QRVZQHAISA-N) is a real dietary/coenzyme B12 form present in BiGGr and is recorded as a declared proxy for the vitamer group, not as an exact identity.
